task.description: WF-02, step 5b, gate, pass 1 of at most 3 — TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on the tests of REQ-106 written at step 5 (handoffs/E2E106-20261115-01/step-05-test-designer.json): tools/test/e2e-stand.test.js, tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js and the new tools/test/e2e/pixel-office.e2e.js, against the block REQ-106 (all 8 criteria), the design docs/design/REQ-106-e2e-pixel-office.md (sections 4.4, 8, 11, 12, 13, 16) and decisions/0112 (О1–О23). Follow the section 'Step 5b' of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md item by item: every criterion has its test and every test asserts what its criterion says, not less (read each assertion yourself); the oracles are independent of the code under test (the README word table and ROLE_NAMES as О15 says); the waits are for facts with limits, no sleep, no wait by time; the replaced assertions of the starter tests keep or strengthen each prohibition (AP-068, AP-112, AP-113); nothing outside the write set changed (compare with the tag and with the hashes of the earlier steps). Mutants: run again at least 15 of the step's list on copies outside the project (a clone of tag base/E2E106-20261115-01 with the run's work files copied in; E2K-61 reads the root README and decisions/0107, so copy those too), including R02, R02h, R02r, S05, S19, S21, P05, P13, P31, P34, P35, and at least eight NEW own mutants that the step's list does not have (of Pixel Office, its hook and page, and of the starter), each with the tests that went red or why it survives and whether that survival is within the criteria. Runs: each changed test alone; the independence loop of the seven spec tests (each name alone: exit 0, exactly one line 'ok 1 - <name>'); npm run -s e2e -- pixel-office three times with duration_ms; a series of at least 20 runs of reconnect alone, under modest load and quiet (AP-115), to show it is not flaky; the kit files three times; the order check on three files; npm run check once at the end. The time of this machine is not the runner's (AP-144). STRICT R2 (rule R2-S of the design, section 6): every call of yours that names the person's home folder or the real Pixel Office state folder goes only to a spawn that records and throws; never import a program file to read it; record sha256, size and time of all five real files before your first trial and after your last. Change no project file other than this handoff; no commit, push or pull. The handoff holds no absolute machine paths, no temporary paths and no names of other projects of the owner. Verdict PASS only if every item of Step 5b holds; otherwise FAIL with findings ranked, each with whether it blocks and the smallest fix.

findings.place: tools/test/e2e/pixel-office.e2e.js, test 'isolated start' part (a): the four runHook refusals and the recorded call; helpers checkedFolder and runHook
findings.what: The real-path handling of the hook helper is not exercised. Every folder the spec gives runHook comes from makeTempDir, which already returns a real path without links, so the assertion that the recorded env holds fs.realpathSync(...) of both folders cannot tell a raw value from the real one: my mutant H01 (runHook checks the folders but gives the hook the raw values) stays green. No refusal case gives a link under the temporary root that points out, so my mutant H02 (the folder checked by its spelling with path.resolve instead of assertUnderTempRoot) passes all four refusal cases and stays green. The same class is covered for the starter (E2S-03 has a link to the home folder; my K03 is red there and green in the spec for the same reason). Criterion 1 is met; the claim of design 4.4 and 8 row 1 ('the recorded hook call has exactly the three variables with the real paths') holds only on inputs where raw and real coincide (AP-110, AP-071 shape). No live risk today: no call gives runHook a link.
findings.fix: In isolated start (a): add one runHook refusal whose office is a symlink made under a folder of the test that points to the real state folder (through the throwing spawn, expect PATH_REFUSED, spawn not called); and make the recorded call with a link and a '..' spelling of the test's own folders, asserting the recorded SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR and HOME equal their real paths. H01 and H02 then go red.

findings.place: tools/test/e2e/pixel-office.e2e.js, isolated start, assert.deepEqual(options.env, { PATH, SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR, HOME })
findings.what: On a red run of a regression that hands the hook the whole environment (the design's mutant R01) this assertion prints the whole environment of the spec process with its values into the TAP output: in my R01 run 52 variables, one of them a variable whose name says it is a token of the session (I deleted that output file at once, I4). The regression itself is caught (isolated start and E2K-50 red), but the red run's log, locally or on the runner, holds the values (Q7 hygiene: a secret does not go into logs; the shape of AP-124).
findings.fix: First assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(options.env).sort(), ['HOME', 'PATH', 'SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR']) so a red message holds names only, then compare the three values one by one.
